name: Book appointments, send reminders, handle no-shows
summary: Works through the appointment book in Calendly: reads each booking into the workflow's book, and queues a yes or no on every finished booking so a person can mark a no-show. Booking a new slot and sending reminders are not covered yet (see gaps). Crons read and queue; a person decides every no-show.

clinic-or-salon-appointments.evidence: 11 calls describe clinic and salon appointments run by hand

covered_by.booking-request: not built (a new booking needs the client's answers, a judgment step)
covered_by.reminder-send: the platform's own reminders (the kit sends none)
covered_by.no-show-handling: no-show (each finished booking queued for a yes or no)

trade-site-bookings.evidence: 3 calls describe site visits booked through an online booking system

unclear.evidence: 12 calls describe bookings with no clear way of working

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Read the next booked appointments from Calendly into the workflow's book.

crons.name: no-show
crons.summary: Queue a yes or no on each finished booking that has no no-show record yet, oldest first, for a person to decide.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations here are reads of scheduled events and their invitees. Nothing the crons read leaves the business. A no-show mark changes a record the client does not see, but it can start the business's own no-show policy, so it is a live operation and waits for a person.

calendly.covers: booked appointments and invitees (read), no-show marks (approval only)

gaps: Cliniko: its appointments, attendee cancel and reminder flags are mapped, but the captured vendor docs show only the equality filter form (q[]=field:=value). A time window (starts_at from and to) needs a comparison filter that is not confirmed, so no adapter is built. Confirm it on a Cliniko trial account, then build the adapter.
Acuity: the evidence names it, but the kit has no Acuity platform folder, so no operations are mapped.

Calendly cannot tell who attended. The no-show cron therefore queues every finished booking for a person to decide, and a rejected one stays rejected. A cron that knows attendance (a clinic system flag such as Cliniko's did_not_arrive) would replace this once that adapter exists.

Booking a new slot (availability-check, book-slot, confirm-booking): not built. It needs the client's answers and a slot choice a person should make. Calendly's invitee create is in the kit but is not a live or draft op of this workflow.

Reminders: the kit sends no reminder. Calendly's own invitee reminders carry this step, and Calendly does not expose whether a reminder went out, so the kit cannot confirm it. Text reminders need an SMS adapter (Twilio, MobileMessage or JustCall have mapped operations here); none is built.
Reschedule and cancel from a client's message: a judgment step. Calendly's cancel is mapped but no cron queues it, so it is not in live_ops yet.
Pagination: each run reads one page of up to 100 events and up to 100 invitees per event. A busy calendar needs the next page followed.

Approval summaries and the run log: each queued summary carries the client's or lead's name, and the runtime logs every summary (core/workflows/runtime.ts). Needs a core change so the runtime logs the approval id only, or the names come out of the summary line.
Stored personal data: invitee names and emails are kept in the workflow's state store. The business needs a retention rule for that store before go-live.
Calendly is docs-only until a sandbox account proves each call. Its sign-in is the CRM's standard Calendly token (CALENDLY_API_TOKEN), not yet run against a real account.

evidence.calls: 40 booking calls read, 26 describe the process: 11 clinic or salon, 3 trade-site, 12 unclear
evidence.platforms: Calendly (72 ops, official spec), Cliniko (223 ops, vendor docs), Acuity (evidence only, no kit folder)
